rounds.text: The current valuation metrics of 0x for P/E, P/B, and EV/EBITDA are mathematically nonsensical and suggest a complete lack of meaningful financial data or a failure in the reporting mechanism [E1, E2, E6]. While recent performance shows high returns, the long-term historical record reveals a persistent pattern of value destruction, with median ROE figures of -3% over ten years, -4% over five years, and -1% over three years [E13, E14, E15]. This historical trend is further corroborated by the explicit flagging of a negative -1.43% ROE over the last three years [E30]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent profitability with an ROE of 18.45% to 20% and a ROCE of 20.54% to 21.6% [E4, E5, E7, E8, E16]. Investors must weigh these recent spikes against the reality that the business has failed to generate positive equity returns for the vast majority of the last decade [E13, E14, E15]. Relying on a single year of performance while ignoring a decade of negative returns presents a significant risk to any thesis built on current profitability [E13, E16].

The bear’s dismissal of the 0x valuation metrics as "nonsensical" ignores the reality that Terraform Realstate Ltd is currently operating with a level of efficiency that dwarfs its sector peers, who struggle with negative returns [E1, E2, E3, E4, E6]. While the bear focuses on historical medians, the most recent data confirms a decisive structural turnaround, with ROE reaching 20% and ROCE hitting 22% [E16, E34, E35]. Conceded: the median ROE over the last three, five, and ten years has been negative [E13, E14, E15, E30]. However, this historical context is secondary to the current evidence showing the company is now generating a ROCE of 20.54% to 21.6%, which significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of 4.38% [E5, E7]. By fixating on past performance, the bear fails to account for the company's current ability to generate returns on assets of 18.33%, compared to the sector's staggering -104.41% [E3]. The evidence demonstrates that the company has successfully pivoted to a high-performance model that renders its long-term historical averages irrelevant to its current operational strength [E4, E5, E16].

The bull’s reliance on "0x" valuation metrics [E1, E2, E6] is mathematically invalid, as a P/E or EV/EBITDA of zero does not represent a bargain but rather a failure to produce meaningful earnings or a lack of reliable data. While the bull highlights recent ROE and ROCE figures [E16, E34, E35], it ignores the persistent, long-term trend of negative returns that define the company's actual track record [E13, E14, E15]. Conceded: the company reported a recent ROE of 20% and ROCE of 21.6% [E16, E7]. However, this single-year spike stands in stark contrast to the 10-year median ROE of -3% and the 3-year median ROE of -1% [E13, E15]. The company’s own filings explicitly flag a low 3-year return on equity of -1.43% as a negative factor, directly contradicting the bull's narrative of a permanent structural turnaround [E30]. Relying on a single year of performance to dismiss a decade of negative returns is a speculative leap that ignores the company's established history of poor capital efficiency [E13, E14, E15, E30].
